analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | CPI | global indu event | bogeys 13 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P futures are roughly flat, but the desk expects large dispersion under the surface. Chip stocks were hit overnight, including Samsung and SK Hynix, which pressures tech shares pre-market. Large bank earnings start this morning.
KOSPI led Asia lower, closing down 546bps at one point after being down as much as 7%. Taiwan fell 195bps and Japan fell 182bps. Europe held up better, with the UK up 75bps and France up 30bps.

Crude is down 150bps, with Brent just below $105 and WTI at $92. Europe gas is up 2% to $86. The 10-year yield is 5.19%, down after the US bond market was closed yesterday. The dollar is lower and Bitcoin is holding $83.5k.
NFIB came in weaker at 97.9 vs 98.2 expected, with a higher prior month. Existing home sales and several Fed speakers are also on today's schedule.

Privo on oil: the Russia/Ukraine energy ceasefire did not survive a news cycle. Trump announced a deal that surprised Kyiv and was never confirmed by Moscow, and Russia struck Ukrainian power infrastructure within hours.

Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport exposed Saudi air defence vulnerabilities, but Brent is lower and production is intact. The market is separating geopolitical escalation from barrels actually lost, which Privo calls reasonable but a fragile equilibrium. Nothing has been agreed on Hormuz.

GS expects September core CPI of +0.24% m/m vs +0.2% consensus, or +2.46% y/y vs +2.5% consensus. Headline CPI is forecast at +0.59% vs +0.6% consensus, driven by higher energy prices. GS's forecast is consistent with a 0.20% rise in September core PCE.

GS expects three component trends in the CPI report: an auto inflation pickup (used cars +0.5%, new cars +0.2%, auto insurance +0.2%), benign shelter (OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%), and airfares +3.0% on higher jet fuel.

GS expects core CPI of about 0.2% in October, with upward pressure from seasonal-factor distortions caused by missing data from last year's government shutdown. It expects about 0.1% in November and December on slowing shelter and shrinking tariff contributions.

Micro news is quiet. One company announced a CFO transition, with Michael Morgan taking over effective November 18, 2026 from Melissa Rasmussen. In Europe, GIVN SW is up on a strong like-for-like sales beat, and SHA0 GR reported preliminary Q3 revenue of EUR5.8bn.

The desk sees mixed checks for aggregates and positive checks for electrical equipment. AZZ reports after the close and FAST reports in the morning. The desk thinks FAST is incrementally shorted, with a 16.5% ADS bogey, and is focused on gross margins and outlook.
Initial bogey requests from clients cover FAST ADS and gross margins, PCAR TP&O gross margins, NVT orders, MMM organic growth, and JBHT intermodal volumes, margins and Q4.
